sections.overview: Echinococcus shiquicus is a small tapeworm described from the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau and recognized as distinct using morphological, ecological and genetic evidence.
sections.identification: It is a cestode in the genus Echinococcus; molecular data distinguish it from the closely related E. multilocularis.
sections.habitat: Published records are from the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, where its known host cycle occurs in high-altitude grassland landscapes.
sections.diet: As a parasite, its larval stage develops in mammalian intermediate hosts and its adult stage inhabits the intestine of a definitive host.
sections.behavior: The established wildlife cycle links Tibetan foxes, which carry adult worms, with plateau pikas, in which larval cysts occur.
sections.reproduction: Like other tapeworms, it produces eggs in its adult host; the documented cycle passes between carnivorous definitive hosts and small-mammal intermediate hosts.
sections.ecology: A 2024 review describes E. shiquicus as a sister taxon to E. multilocularis and reports its records from the Tibetan Plateau.
sections.conservation: The parasite sources consulted discuss host ecology and public-health uncertainty rather than assigning this species a conservation category.
